comments.text:
Alex Preti was an ICU nurse.

I am also a nurse.

The American Nurses Association has a Code of Ethics with 10 Provisions that all nurses are meant to follow. Nurses have many roles - we are educators, we are part of an intradisciplinary team, we are healers, we are holistic (meaning "whole person") and patient-centered caregivers - but one of our biggest roles is being *advocates*, speaking up for our patients, for their families, and our community.

Provision 9 of the ANA's Code of Ethics states:

"Nurses and their professional organizations work to enact and resource practices, policies, and legislation to promote social justice, eliminate health inequities, and facilitate human flourishing."

It is not enough as a nurse to stand idly by and wring our hands while people, people in our community, are suffering. Alex Preti embodied Provision 9, and he even put his life on the line to do so. He served his community in a myriad of ways. As a fellow nurse, I'm heartbroken and sickened at this disgusting violence inflicted on one of my own, especially when he was doing his job and advocating for his community.
